To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of water to the toluene-based AOT microemulsions results in the formation of bidisperse colloidal systems in which silica nanoparticles coexist with a second population of AOT microemulsion droplet.

the addition of water to a silica nanoparticle dispersion in AOT-toluene leads to the formation of mixed systems in which the nanoparticles coexist with a new population of microemulsion droplet structures.

the addition of water to the AOT/toluene/silica system results in the formation of mixed hard/soft colloidal structures in which the hard components are 80 nm silica nanoparticles and the soft components are 10 nm microemulsion droplet structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the preparation, characterisation and understanding of the structure of novel mixed 'hard-soft colloidal systems' in which the'soft' components are inverse microemulsion droplet structures and the 'hard' component is a dispersion of silica nanoparticles.
the preparation and characterisation of novel mixed 'hard-soft colloidal systems' which have potential application in the areas of nanotechnology and drug delivery.
the development of a new class of colloids that have both hard and soft components, with the potential to provide a new route to the design of novel materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these are novel and exciting colloidal systems, which are of great interest to the scientific community, and that the authors should be congratulated on their work.

the addition of water to AOT-stabilised toluene colloidal systems leads to the formation of two populations of colloidal objects: silica nanoparticles, and microemulsion droplet structures, which can coexist in a stable state.

the addition of water to the toluene-based AOT system leads to the formation of microemulsions with the formation of a bimodal distribution of structures, i.e. the coexistence of nanoparticles and microemulsion droplet populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of water to a silica nanoparticle dispersion containing a high concentration of AOT stabilises the nanoparticles by the formation of mixed 'hard-soft', bidisperse, colloidal systems in which the'soft' component consists of microemulsion droplet structures.
the addition of water to the AOT/toluene system leads to a coexistence of two types of particles: silica nanoparticles and swollen microemulsions, both stabilised by the AOT surfactant.

the addition of water to the silica nanoparticles in the presence of AOT and toluene, leads to an increase in the attractive interactions between the nanoparticles and to the formation of a mixed colloidal system in which both silica nanoparticles and microemulsion droplet structures coexist.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these mixed systems are not simple superpositions of their individual constituents, but exhibit new properties and behaviours.
the silica particles can coexist with microemulsions without significant interaction.
the silica nanoparticles are stabilised in the toluene-AOT-water system by the AOT surfactant and not by the toluene solvent.
